evals.name: audit-flawed-skill
evals.prompt: Audit the supplied deploy-helper skill folder. Write your findings to <outputs>/audit.md as a prioritized list; for each finding say what is wrong, why it matters, and the concrete fix.
evals.expected_output: A prioritized audit report that catches the planted defects, contains no false positives, reports validator results, and proposes a description with a trigger clause, indirect cases, and a boundary.
assertions: Flags that the name `deploy_helper` is invalid (underscore) AND that it does not match the folder `deploy-helper`
Flags that the description 'Helps with deployments.' lacks trigger conditions, and the proposed replacement contains a semantic trigger clause, at least one indirect phrasing, and a boundary clause
Flags the body 'When to Use' section as unable to affect auto-triggering and says trigger text belongs in the description
Flags the staging/production contradiction AND resolves it as an explicit conditional rule (hotfix vs. normal) rather than just deleting one side
Flags the migrations contradiction (NEVER run vs. deploy script runs them) and proposes a resolution
Flags the time-relative Q3 2026 instruction and recommends stating the current method with legacy collapsed
Flags the missing referenced file references/gcp.md
Flags the ungated 'See references/ for details' pointer AND the reference chain aws.md -> aws-iam.md, recommending gating by condition and one level deep
Flags the Kubernetes/Helm background paragraph as known to the agent (wasted tokens)
Flags the tool menu (kubectl / helm / deploy script) and recommends a single default with a gated alternative
Flags that the /health gotcha buried in references/aws.md contradicts the body's verification step and recommends moving it into SKILL.md
Reports the output of the structural validator (validate_skill.py or equivalent) as part of the audit
Contains no false-positive findings: does not report as broken anything that is valid under skill-root-relative resolution (e.g., the aws.md -> aws-iam.md link path itself)
Findings are ordered with behavior-affecting contradictions ranked above formatting/convention issues

evals.name: create-branching-release-skill
evals.prompt: Create a project skill for our release process in <fixture>/.cursor/skills/. The process differs by what changed: for anything under packages/* we use changesets (`yarn changeset`, but it's interactive so the file has to be written by hand; core packages are version-linked so bumping one bumps them all; internal-only changes get no changeset); for examples/* there is no release but the example's lockfile must be refreshed with `yarn install --mode=update-lockfile`; for website/ we run `yarn workspace rdc-website build` and then `netlify deploy --prod`; docs-only changes just need `yarn workspace rdc-website typecheck` to pass. It should kick in automatically whenever someone talks about releasing, publishing, shipping, or cutting a version, even if they don't say 'release'. Write it as a complete skill folder.
evals.expected_output: A concise skill folder whose SKILL.md has valid frontmatter, a description with trigger clause and indirect phrasings, the four-way branch encoded once as a decision table, gotchas in the body, gated concept-named reference links, exact commands from the prompt, and nothing the prompt did not ask for.
assertions: A SKILL.md exists in a folder whose name equals the frontmatter `name`, and the name is lowercase-hyphenated
The description contains a semantic trigger clause that names release/publish/ship/version and at least one indirect case (e.g., 'even if they don't say release')
The four branches (packages, examples, website, docs-only) are encoded as a table or explicit condition -> action structure
Each branch's procedure is encoded once; the same branch logic does not appear again as prose subsections and again as a checklist
The SKILL.md body is at most 70 lines
There is no 'When to Use' section in the body
The version-linked core packages fact appears as a gotcha or equivalent explicit correction in SKILL.md
The packages branch says `yarn changeset` is interactive and directs the agent to write the changeset file manually instead of running the command
The packages branch says internal-only changes receive no changeset
The body does not explain what changesets, Netlify, or lockfiles are

All four non-interactive branch commands appear exactly as given in the prompt (`yarn install --mode=update-lockfile`, `yarn workspace rdc-website build`, `netlify deploy --prod`, `yarn workspace rdc-website typecheck`)
Any reference files live under references/, are introduced with a condition, and are linked as [Concept Name](references/file.md) with concept text rather than the path; if none exist, this passes
No procedures or rules are added beyond what the prompt specified (e.g., no invented CI steps, status commands, or docs-in-same-PR rules)
There are no ALL-CAPS MUST/NEVER directives without an accompanying reason
The skill's own `scripts/validate_skill.py`, run against the created folder, exits 0 with no convention warnings
